description:
SPACENESIS is an interdisciplinary team of Biomedical students united by a passion for bioscience, technology, and space exploration.

We are developing a smart health-monitoring application designed to help astronauts track their physical and mental health during space missions. 

SPACENESIS — Exploring Space, Understanding Life, Protecting Health.
summary:
SPACENESIS is a web app for spaceflight health monitoring. It lets astronauts check on their own health and spot changes early during missions beyond Earth.

Users start with a daily check-in covering sleep, mood, stress, focus and symptoms. They can then review health indicators such as heart rate, blood oxygen, sleep quality and stress. The app tracks body systems in a monitoring plan (cardiovascular, respiratory, immune and skeletal). It also shows vital sign trends over time, tracks bone-health countermeasures, and has an Emergency Support section that guides the crew to the next safe step based on approved mission procedures. A Space Environment module and an interactive Human Atlas help users understand how the body responds in space.

The challenge is that astronauts work far from hospitals and spaceflight affects many body systems at once. SPACENESIS puts their health data in one clear, easy-to-use place. It is a working prototype that uses sample data and is designed to support, not replace, flight medical teams.
details: SPACENESIS is a web app that helps astronauts monitor their health on missions beyond Earth. Crew members complete a daily check-in covering sleep, mood, stress, focus and symptoms. They can then review health indicators such as heart rate, blood oxygen, sleep quality and stress, and track the cardiovascular, respiratory, immune and skeletal systems in a monitoring plan. The app shows vital sign trends over time, logs bone-health countermeasures, and has an Emergency Support section that points the crew to the next safe step based on approved mission procedures. A 3D crew atlas lets users select an astronaut in the rocket and rotate a 3D body. Organs with a flagged change, such as a kidney, turn red. Benefits and impact: Astronauts work far from hospitals, and microgravity, radiation, isolation and disrupted sleep affect many body systems at once. SPACENESIS puts this information in one clear place so changes can be noticed early. It is designed to support flight medical teams, not replace them.
